title: Move Chat into Side Bar silently loses imported chats
body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

Version: 1.134.0-insider (user setup)
Commit: f844934f854c9277a48627aac77ebcea69591ae1
Date: 2026-08-11T22:56:11Z
Electron: 42.8.0
ElectronBuildId: 14845705
Chromium: 148.0.7778.280
Node.js: 24.18.0
V8: 14.8.178.38-electron.0
@github/copilot: 1.0.79-9
@github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.10-preview.0
OS: f844934f854c9277a48627aac77ebcea69591ae1

The bug report below was created by Copilot (GPT-5.6 Sol). I hit the bug originally and verified the reduced repro steps. The original bug repro was not through an import, but via a new chat that later on disappeared (Copilot was able to recover it from disk with a .json I can import for the chat).

### Summary

After using `Chat: Import Chat...`, the imported conversation opens correctly
in a Chat editor. Selecting **Move Chat into Secondary Side Bar** closes the
editor, but the imported conversation does not appear in the Chat view and is
no longer accessible without importing the JSON again.

This reproduces with a 25-character title, so title length is unrelated.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Save the attached `repro-imported-chat-move.json`.
```json
{
  "responderUsername": "GitHub Copilot",
  "requests": [
    {
      "requestId": "request_repro_1",
      "message": "Short imported chat title",
      "variableData": {
        "variables": []
      },
      "response": [
        {
          "value": "This is a synthetic imported chat used to reproduce a session move issue."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```
3. Run **Chat: Import Chat...** and select the file.
4. Confirm that its request and response appear in the Chat editor.
5. Select **Move Chat into Secondary Side Bar** from the editor title actions.
### Actual Behavior

The Chat editor closes and the imported conversation disappears. It is not
shown in the destination Chat view, Sessions list, or Show Chats.

There is no error notification. Clicking New Session does not recover it.

### Expected Behavior

The imported conversation should remain visible in the destination Chat view.

If imported chats are intentionally editor-only, the move actions should be
disabled for them instead of silently discarding the conversation.

### Source-Level Diagnosis

In `chatMoveActions.ts`, `moveToSidebar` does the following in this order:

```ts
await editorService.closeEditor(...);
view = await viewsService.openView(ChatViewId);
const newModel = await view.loadSession(chatEditorInput.sessionResource);
```

Closing the source editor releases its model reference before the destination
tries to acquire it.

In `chatServiceImpl.ts`, imported chats are intentionally excluded from
persistence:

```ts
return session.initialLocation === ChatAgentLocation.Chat
    && !session.isImported;
```

They are also excluded from session history:

```ts
return !entry.isImported && !entry.isDeleted && ...;
```

Therefore, when closing the editor releases the imported model's final
reference, there is neither a live model nor persisted session data for
`view.loadSession(...)` to recover.

Potential fixes include:

- Acquire and retain the model before closing the source editor, releasing that
  reference only after the destination has acquired it.
- Convert the imported model into a persistable local session during the move.
- Disable the move actions for imported chats and explain that they are
  editor-only.

### Environment

- VS Code: `1.134.0-insider`
- Commit: `f844934f854c9277a48627aac77ebcea69591ae1`
- GitHub Copilot Chat: `0.62.2026081101`
- Windows 11 25H2, build `26200`
- WSL2, Ubuntu 26.04
- Multi-root workspace

title: Chat sessions: expose provider-defined sticky session details in the chat editor
body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

## Feature request

Allow chat session providers to publish structured, dynamic session details that VS Code renders in a compact sticky section at the top of the chat editor.

## Motivation

`ChatSessionItem.metadata` supports arbitrary JSON-serializable data, but VS Code does not render it. `description` and `badge` are primarily session-list properties.

Providers currently have to include session state in model-generated Markdown. This has several drawbacks:

- It consumes model context and output tokens.
- It is repeated in every response.
- It scrolls out of view.
- It can become inconsistent with provider-owned state.

Useful session-level details include:

- Topic or task
- Current step
- Pull request link and state
- Suggested next steps
- Branch, environment, or deployment state

## Proposed UX

For sessions that provide details, display a compact section below the session title and above the transcript.

- Keep it visible while the transcript scrolls.
- Update values without adding a chat turn.
- Allow users to collapse the section.
- Preserve collapsed state per session.
- Support links where appropriate.
- Hide the section when no details are provided.
- Remain accessible and usable at narrow editor widths.

## Illustrative API

```ts
interface ChatSessionItem {
  details?: readonly ChatSessionDetail[];
}

interface ChatSessionDetail {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly label: string;
  readonly value: string | MarkdownString;
  readonly iconPath?: ThemeIcon;
  readonly target?: Uri | Command;
}
```

For example:

```ts
item.details = [
  { id: 'step', label: 'Current Step', value: 'Running targeted tests' },
  {
    id: 'pr',
    label: 'Pull Request',
    value: 'Open',
    target: Uri.parse('https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/123')
  }
];
```

The exact API shape is only illustrative. Updating the details should refresh the existing session UI without recreating the session.

## Ownership and safety

- Providers should only update details for sessions they own.
- Arbitrary `metadata` should remain opaque and should not be rendered automatically.
- Only explicitly provided detail fields should appear.
- Markdown and link handling should follow existing chat trust and sanitization rules.

## Related issues

- #327671 requests read access to session status owned by other providers.
- #325507 requests observable agent and subagent lifecycle information.
- #268063 tracked broader chat-session API design work.

This proposal is complementary: it provides a provider-to-user presentation surface for dynamic session-level information.

title: fix: raise mocha timeout for AgentSdkDownloader tests (build fix for vscode-engineering#3401)

labels.name: vscode-build
labels.description: VS Code build process issues

body:
## Build failure

The Windows `Run unit tests (node.js)` stage failed because several node.js
unit tests in `vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/` exceeded mocha's default
2000ms timeout, e.g.:

- `AgentSdkDownloader loadSdkRoot: reports monotonic download progress ending at totalBytes`
- `AgentSdkDownloader loadSdkRoot: cache hit returns immediately without re-downloading`
- `AgentSdkDownloader loadSdkRoot: cache dir includes sdkTarget so Universal launches stay separate`
- `AgentSdkDownloader loadSdkRoot: concurrent calls in same process share one download`

Error: `Timeout of 2000ms exceeded. (vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSdkDownloader.test)`

## Root cause

The `AgentSdkDownloader` integration suite exercises the real
network → cache → extract flow: each test spins up a loopback HTTP server,
downloads a gzip tarball, and extracts it to disk via `tar`. That work
routinely takes longer than mocha's 2000ms default on Windows CI (disk
I/O, AV scanning, and gzip extraction are all slower there), so the tests
flake with timeouts even though no product code changed. The suite ran on
the default timeout with no explicit headroom; only the long-running
"cancel before download completes" test opted into a longer timeout locally.

The sibling `SessionDatabase initialization retries after a transient
initialization failure` test already carries an explicit `.timeout(10_000)`
on `main`, so no change is needed there.

## How the fix works

Adds a suite-level `this.timeout(20_000)` to the `AgentSdkDownloader`
integration suite by converting the suite callback to a `function`
expression (so `this` binds to the mocha suite context). This applies to
every test in the suite while preserving the existing per-test
`this.timeout(15_000)` override on the cancellation test. The change is
test-only and does not alter any production behavior, telemetry, or error
handling.

## Validation

Static/source inspection only. The environment available to this change
cannot run the VS Code node.js unit-test suite (`scripts/test.sh`) to
completion, so the timeout increase was verified by source review: the
suite now propagates a 20s timeout to all of its tests via mocha's
suite-level `this.timeout`, matching the established pattern used by other
long-running suites in this directory (e.g.
`copilotSdkImportSession.integrationTest.ts`).

## Risk

Very low. The change only raises the allowed wall-clock time for existing
tests; it cannot mask a real product regression because these tests still
assert the same behavior and will still fail if the downloader misbehaves.
A genuinely hung download is still caught by the dedicated cancellation
test and CI's overall job timeout.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@Giuspepe`

## Summary

Adds a once-per-local-client `agentHost.startup` product telemetry event covering the Agent Host startup path through the first successful session list.

The event records bounded client/connection context and durations for:

- initial MessagePort acquisition
- AHP protocol connection
- initial authentication settlement
- first session-list request and successful completion
- session-list attempt and failure counts

title: Chat input stack: make the notice/input seam structural instead of per-surface offsets

labels.name: debt
labels.description: Code quality issues

labels.name: ux
labels.description: User experience issues

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
Follow-up to #330307, which unified how the five notices above a chat input *look* (one base widget, one stylesheet). That change deliberately left one thing alone, and this issue is about fixing it properly: **how far each notice sits from the input below it.**

## Problem

A notice has a square bottom edge; the chat input has rounded top corners. Sat flush, the input's rounding leaves gaps at the corners and the two borders read as a seam. So each surface pulls the input up over the notice's bottom edge to hide the join.

The number is different everywhere. Measured against `main`:

| offset | surface |
| --- | --- |
| −8px | sessions homepage, notification |
| −6px | workbench panel, notification |
| −4px | workbench compact, getting-started tip |
| 0 | workbench panel tip, sessions tip, sub-session tip |
| +4px | voice and dictation introductions |
| +16px | inline chat, notification (a deliberate gap) |

The reason it cannot be one value is structural: **the notices are not adjacent to the input.** The flat layout puts thirteen slots above it, four of which sit *between* the last notice and the input:

```
… → notification → voice → dictation → goal-banner → todo-list
  → artifacts → editing-session → getting-started-tip → INPUT
```

So which widget actually touches the input depends on which ones are present. The current answer is adjacency arithmetic: **11 negative margins across 7 stylesheets**, each widget squaring its own corners, plus a five-selector `:has()` block in `chat.css` that squares the input's top whenever any of five widgets appears.

That block also conflicts with our own guidance — `.github/instructions/css-best-practices.instructions.md` says to avoid `:has()` and use an explicit marker class instead.

### Sharing the offset does not work, and has now failed twice

Both attempts happened during #330307 and were reverted:

1. A shared offset on the notice lane **slipped past existing per-surface overrides**, which only ever set `margin-bottom`, leaving 10px of dead space in two surfaces.
2. Splitting a hide/show pair across two files produced **equally specific rules**, so whichever stylesheet loaded last won, and the voice card could render `display: none`.

The lesson is that the offset is not a property of the notice at all. It is a property of the stack it sits in.

## Proposal

One container holds every above-input widget **and** the input:

- `display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0`
- the border and the radius live on the **container**, with `overflow: hidden`
- children draw no radius and no adjoining border of their own

Then the seam disappears structurally. No negative margins, no corner-squaring rules, no presence checks. Adding or removing a widget is automatic, and the eight widget families stop needing to know about each other.

## How this works if notices appear outside the input

Worth stating explicitly, because it shapes the design.

Two of the three layers already generalise:

- **Arbitration.** `ChatInputNoticeHubService` is already a window-level registry: it holds a set of hosts, tracks recency, and routes focus to whichever is active. Each area gets a host; lanes and claims are per-host. Nothing here assumes an input.
- **Appearance.** `.chat-input-notice` already describes what a notice looks like independently of where it is docked.

The part that does **not** generalise today is the seam assumption baked into the shared frame: `border-bottom: none` plus squared bottom corners assume there is an input directly below. A notice rendered anywhere else would have an open bottom edge.

This proposal fixes that, because it moves the seam decision from the notice to its container:

- a notice **inside a stack** — the container clips and draws the frame, so children join seamlessly with no per-notice rules
- a notice **anywhere else** — keeps its own complete frame, because nothing told it otherwise

In other words the notice stops describing its neighbours, and the container describes the join. That is what makes a second location cheap: a new host plus a normal container, with no new offsets to tune.

If notices do become general, the `chatInput*` naming should follow — `ChatNoticeWidget`, `ChatNoticeHost`, `.chat-notice` — since the input would be one host among several.

## Scope: every participant in the stack

The seam is currently handled by whichever widgets happen to be present, so the work is spread across the whole stack, not just the notices.

**Already unified by #330307 — no work needed here**

| widget | where |
| --- | --- |
| notification | `chatInputNotificationWidget.css`, `chatInput.css` (sessions) |
| voice introduction | `voiceModeOnboarding.css` |
| dictation introduction | `dictationOnboarding.css` |
| getting-started tip | `chatTipContent.css` |
| sub-session tip | `newChatInSession.css` |

**Not yet touched — this is the actual work**

| widget | seam handling today |
| --- | --- |
| goal banner | `margin-bottom: -10px` (`chatGoalBannerWidget.css`) |
| editing session | `margin-bottom: -4px` + `:has()` corner squaring (`chat.css`) |
| artifacts | `margin-bottom: -4px` + `:has()` corner squaring (`chat.css`) |
| todo list | `margin-bottom: -4px` + `:has()` corner squaring, plus an adjacency rule keyed on the notification (`chat.css`) |
| sessions feedback banner | `margin-bottom: calc(-1 * size80)` (`chatInput.css`) |

**Dead, and should go with it**

`chat-input-widgets-container` and `chat-status-widget` have **zero TypeScript references** anywhere in `src/`, yet still occupy a negative-margin rule and one of the five `:has()` selectors in `chat.css`.

**In the stack but with no seam handling today**

Persistent content, plan review, question carousel, tool confirmation carousel and followups. No rules to delete, but a restructure changes how they lay out, so they need verifying.

## Risk

- Main risk is `overflow: hidden` on the container clipping overflow widgets. Partly precedented: the sessions composer already mounts editor overflow widgets on the workbench container to avoid exactly this.
- Needs verification per surface. #330307 used a Playwright harness comparing computed offsets across nine notice×surface combinations against `main`; the same approach applies and should be extended to cover the widgets above.
- Removing the `:has()` block also brings `chat.css` in line with `.github/instructions/css-best-practices.instructions.md`.

## Why this is separate from #330307

#330307 is presentation unification for five producers and is deletion-heavy. This is a structural change to the whole input stack whose main risk is layout regressions in widgets that have nothing to do with notices. Landing #330307 first makes this cheaper: the four notices now share one frame rule, so there are four fewer things to reason about.
